record.provider: Ghost(Pro) — 5 MB on free trial/Starter, 100 MB Publisher; self-hosted is unbounded

free_tier.stated: "When uploading media files to Ghost, while there is no limit on the number of files you can upload to your site, there is a file size limit based on your Ghost(Pro) plan. Free trial: 5mb / Starter: 5mb / Publisher: 100mb / Business: 250mb / Custom: 1gb"

egress.terms: CDN-served; free tier has no egress billing. Fair Use Policy applies to media hosting.

record.tooling: Ghost Content API + Admin API (REST), official JS SDK. Self-hosted Ghost has no file-count or size limit except the web server config: "The upload limit is effectively determined by the web server that's serving your Ghost site."
record.chaining: The interesting half is not Ghost(Pro). It is that Ghost's unlimited-file design means a self-hosted Ghost on any free host inherits an unbounded media library. That chains Ghost's admin API to whatever free compute/storage is already available, rather than being storage itself.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap 5 MB (free/Starter), 100 MB (Publisher), 250 MB (Business), 1 GB (Custom). No file-count cap on any plan. Ghost Fair Use Policy constrains 'other file types made available'. Enforcement is the practical ceiling.
record.reliability_note: Ghost(Pro) free trial expires; the unlimited-file behaviour only persists on a paid plan or self-hosted install.

evidence.proved: per-plan 5mb/100mb/250mb/1gb table, "no limit on the number of files"
limit is the web server's on self-hosted
